title: Compact Modern Home
challenge: The Manjunath family had a 30x40 site in Hoskote Town and wanted a striking, low-maintenance elevation without compromising on natural light inside — a common tension on compact plots where street-facing walls can end up blocking cross-ventilation.
approach: We designed a geometric blue-grey facade with vertical slit windows positioned to pull light and air through the home without sacrificing street-side privacy — a detail that matters on a narrow plot where windows often face a neighbouring wall.
outcome: Delivered as G+1 with a terrace utility room, geometric blue-grey facade, vertical slit windows for cross-ventilation, and a palm-shaded sit-out that keeps the entrance cool through Hoskote's summer months.

title: Premium Façade Villa
challenge: The Prakash family wanted their home to stand out after dark as much as in daylight — a request that shapes design decisions most homeowners never think about until they're standing outside their own house at 9pm wondering why it looks flat.
approach: We built the elevation around a warm wood-and-stone material palette that reads differently under daylight versus designer facade lighting, using wooden accent paneling and a frameless glass balcony railing so the structure itself, not just added fixtures, does the visual work at night.
outcome: Delivered as G+2 on a 30x50 site with designer façade lighting, wooden accent paneling, frameless glass balcony railing, and a covered car porch with false ceiling.
imgalt: G+2 premium wood and stone facade villa Hoskote, night view
floors_desc_short: ground floor plus two upper floors

title: Narrow-Plot Tower Home
challenge: The Srinivas family had a 30x40 frontage plot and wanted a G+2 home that still felt spacious and modern — a real design challenge, since stacking three floors on a narrow footprint can easily end up feeling like a tower rather than a home.
approach: We used a navy-trim geometric elevation with wood-panel accent windows to break up the building's height visually, and mirrored balcony placement on both upper floors so the massing reads as intentional rather than simply tall.
outcome: Delivered as G+2 on a 30x40 plot with a navy-trim geometric elevation, wood-panel accent windows, and matching balconies on both floors.
imgalt: G+2 navy trim tower home Hoskote, narrow plot
floors_desc_short: ground floor plus two upper floors

title: Commercial + Residential Building
challenge: The Nagaraj family wanted their 30x50 site to work harder than a purely residential build — ground-floor shop space for rental income, with two full residential floors above for the family itself.
approach: This meant designing to two different standards at once: commercial-grade shuttering and access for the ground floor, and a genuinely livable residential layout above it — with structural planning that accounts for a heavier, more varied load pattern than a purely residential G+2 would need.
outcome: Delivered as G+3 on a 30x50 plot — ground-floor commercial shutters, two stone-clad residential floors above, and a terrace utility area.
imgalt: G+3 commercial and residential stone-clad building Hoskote, housewarming
floors_desc_short: ground-floor commercial space plus three residential floors
timeline: 18–24 months (extended for the commercial ground-floor fit-out)

title: Contemporary Single-Floor Home
challenge: The Ravindra family wanted a clean, modern look on a 30x40 plot without stretching their budget — proof that a striking elevation and the Comfortable package aren't mutually exclusive if the design decisions are the right ones.
approach: Rather than spreading the budget thin across many decorative elements, we concentrated it on one standout feature — a decorative stone accent panel — paired with an exposed-brick balcony and a steel-grille car porch gate that reads as intentional, not cost-cut.
outcome: Delivered as G+1 on a 30x40 plot with an exposed-brick balcony, decorative stone accent panel, and steel-grille car porch gate.
imgalt: G+1 cream house with brown stone accent panel Hoskote

title: Open-Porch Family Home
challenge: The Chandrashekar family prioritized a large open car porch on their 30x50 site — building for how the family actually lives day to day, rather than maximizing built-up area for its own sake.
approach: We designed a curved parapet and brick-pattern window trim to give the elevation character despite the generous open porch area, and added wooden-louvre windows and an elevated water tank structure that keep the utility elements from looking like an afterthought.
outcome: Delivered as G+1 on a 30x50 plot with a curved parapet design, brick-pattern window trim, wooden-louvre windows, and an elevated water tank structure.
